Risk Weight Simulator

Risk Weight Simulator

Effects of replacing the internal ratings-based (IRBA) risk weights on corporate loans with an alternative schedule. Based on the German calibration in Maximilian Jager and Karl Schulz, Nonlinear Bank Capital Regulation (2026). Competitive banking; all effects are measured relative to the current IRBA schedule.

Methodology

First order. Gateaux derivatives at the IRBA schedule, applied to the full schedule change. First-order welfare is linear in the change, so it scales with the size of the reform.

Large reform. The reform is split into N steps, and at each step every loan solves its credit and risk response. Results are extrapolated to N → ∞ from N and N/2 steps.

Best simple schedules. The flat, two-rating, linear and isoelastic schedules with the highest welfare at the baseline calibration. Two ratings weights each borrower by its investment-grade share. Under changed assumptions they keep these parameters.

Optimal schedule. The risk weight of each loan equals the marginal welfare externality of its credit, b(p), shown in Figure A4.

Numerical checks. A reform is marked invalid when its schedule sets negative risk weights, its step equation fails to converge, the denominator of its step update turns zero or negative, or a result is infinite. PD is capped at 100%.

Baseline calibration. ζk,ω = −0.349 (reform-based estimate). Baseline values: F(z*) = 5%, κT = 0.3, investment-grade share 57%, loan rate r = 4.68%, depreciation rate ι = 0.1965. Fixed: f(z*) = 1.2, ζk,ω′ = 0 (estimated value 0.001). Figures show p up to 10%; the PD grid runs to 50%.
